Hi, I don't understand why `needToClose` is here? If someone destroys the stream we need to always close the generator don't we?

That is - if someone creates a stream, calls `.read` but `.next` is never called on the generator - `needToClose` is false and blocks don't run (since await iterator.next()` is async and waits a microtick)

issue_context.title: stream.Readable.from does not always close synchronous generators
issue_context.body:
<!--
Thank you for reporting an issue.

This issue tracker is for bugs and issues found within Node.js core.
If you require more general support please file an issue on our help
repo. https://github.com/nodejs/help


Please fill in as much of the template below as you're able.

Version: output of `node -v`
Platform: output of `uname -a` (UNIX), or version and 32 or 64-bit (Windows)
Subsystem: if known, please specify affected core module name
-->

* **Version**: 12.16.2, 13.12.0
* **Platform**: linux
* **Subsystem**: arch

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

<!--
Enter details about your bug, preferably a simple code snippet that can be
run using `node` directly without installing third-party dependencies.
-->
If synchronous generator wrapped with `stream.Readable.from` emits rejected `Promise` then finally blocks of that generator is never called.
But if that generator is consumed with general `for-of` loop then `finally` blocks are called as expected.

```js
stream.Readable.from(function*() {
  try {
    yield Promise.resolve(1)
    yield Promise.reject('error')
  } finally {
    console.log('fin')
  }
}())
.on('data',x=>console.log(x))
.on('error',e=>console.log(e))
```

It logs
```
1
error
```
but does not log `fin`.

### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?

Always.

### What is the expected behavior?

`stream.Readable.from` should either not resolve `Promise`s yielded from synchronous generators and should pass unresolved `Promise`s to the returned stream or should properly close generator even if it yields rejected `Promise`.


### Additional information

<!--
Tell us anything else you think we should know.
-->
To fix this there should be called `iterator.return` if `await value` throws.
https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/f21cf456bf36bd73d8cb6715c745e23efc22a29f/lib/internal/streams/from.js#L57

<!--
I guess this happens because `stream.Readable.from` uses `for-await-of` loop for consuming both synchronous and asynchronous generators. According to [ECMAScript specification](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-%asyncfromsynciteratorprototype%.next) `for-await-of` loop closes synchronous generator only if it yields general values or resolved thenables, but not rejected thenables.

I think that `stream.Readable.from` should consume generators with appropriate `for-of` loop. Synchronous generators - with synchronous `for-of`, asynchronous generators - with asynchronous `for-await-of` loop.

Another option could be to point out in the documentation that `stream.Readable.from` uses `for-await-of` loop under the hood to consume all the type of generators and so has the same restrictions as that loop.
-->
